# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: Stops `TypeCollector` from crashing on a closed generic value type that comes from a referenced assembly. It does three things. (1) All analyzer diagnostics now go through a new filter, `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`, which drops any diagnostic whose location is not a source tree in the current compilation. (2) The MemberNeedsKey site now uses `FirstOrDefault()` instead of indexing `[0]`. (3) The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull site now calls a new helper, `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation`, but that helper still indexes `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. Three tests compile a library to metadata and then check two things: the consumer builds with no diagnostics, and a resolver is generated. README and the MsgPack004 doc gain prose describing the new suppression policy.
story.why: Issue #2283: the generator (CS8785) and analyzer (AD0001) throw IndexOutOfRangeException because metadata symbols have no `DeclaringSyntaxReferences`. As a result the consuming assembly silently gets no generated resolver.
touches_beyond_requirement: A global diagnostic filter (line 239/1444-1450) that silently drops every diagnostic with no in-compilation source location, not just ones about metadata types.
README section and MsgPack004.md section documenting a new diagnostic-suppression policy.
story.confidence_overview: Medium that the reported repro is fixed: the tests mirror the issue's code and assert that a resolver is generated. Low on completeness. The issue names three crashing `[0]` sites. One is truly fixed (1077). One is wrapped in a helper whose doc comment says it returns null for metadata, but its body still indexes `[0]` (1434). The third (~line 735 in the original) does not appear in the diff. The broad location filter is a behavior change to existing analyzer rules that the human should weigh.

claims.text: The new tests reproduce the issue's scenario. Each compiles the defining code to a metadata-only image, references it from the consumer, and asserts both that no warning/error diagnostics are produced and that the resolver hint name appears in generator output.
claims.requirement_quote: A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

breaker.reason: At GenericsFormatterTests.cs line 667, CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync calls compilation.Emit(stream) with default EmitOptions, which emits a full PE assembly with IL rather than a metadata-only reference image (EmitOptions(emitMetadataOnly: true)), and only wraps that full PE image via MetadataReference.CreateFromImage (line 673). In REQ-2283's ProjectReference build, MSBuild passes a reference assembly (where Roslyn synthesizes non-CompilerGenerated dummy fields on structs) and runs MessagePackGenerator on the defining project; CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync does neither.

breaker.reason: Checked TypeCollector.cs line 1077: MemberNeedsKey now uses item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation(), which evaluates to null (Location.None in Diagnostic.Create) instead of throwing IndexOutOfRangeException when DeclaringSyntaxReferences is empty on a metadata symbol, and ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember exercises this path.

claims.text: Every analyzer diagnostic is now filtered: it is reported only if its location is in source and its syntax tree belongs to the current compilation. All others, including diagnostics created with a null location, are silently dropped.

breaker.reason: TypeCollector.cs line 239 wraps the reportAnalyzerDiagnostic callback passed to this private TypeCollector constructor in ReportIfLocatedInCompilation (lines 1444-1450), which drops any diagnostic whose Location is not in a syntax tree belonging to this.compilation (including Location.None from a null location). However, MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs and lines 1-234 of TypeCollector.cs are not in the diff, so we cannot verify from the diff alone whether every analyzer diagnostic goes through this single delegate rather than being reported directly on SymbolAnalysisContext or via another path.

claims.text: The tests skip generated-source content checks (`SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck`) and only assert the resolver hint name. They do not verify that a formatter for the closed generic struct is emitted or correct.

breaker.reason: Checked GenericsFormatterTests.cs lines 641 and 656-658: VerifyCS.Test sets TestBehaviors.SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck, and the manual CSharpGeneratorDriver check only asserts no warning/error diagnostics and that expectedResolverHintName is in hintNames, without inspecting generated source text or testing serialization to confirm a formatter for the closed generic struct was actually emitted and registered.

refusals.what: Existing analyzer rules (e.g. MsgPack004 MemberNeedsKey) now silently suppress any diagnostic without an in-compilation source location.
refusals.why: This changes user-visible analyzer behavior and may hide diagnostics users previously saw; S4 only checks for new rule descriptors.

refusals.what: `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation`'s doc comment says it returns null for metadata properties, but the implementation still indexes `[0]`.
refusals.why: The comment misstates behavior and leaves one of the crash sites named in the issue unfixed.

refusals.what: README and MsgPack004.md document a new diagnostic-suppression policy that the requirement did not ask for.
refusals.why: These are documentation changes beyond the requirement, and they assert a guarantee (reporting by the defining assembly) that is not always true.

findings.description: Claim C4 disputed: At GenericsFormatterTests.cs line 667, CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync calls compilation.Emit(stream) with default EmitOptions, which emits a full PE assembly with IL rather than a metadata-only reference image (EmitOptions(emitMetadataOnly: true)), and only wraps that full PE image via MetadataReference.CreateFromImage (line 673). In REQ-2283's ProjectReference build, MSBuild passes a reference assembly (where Roslyn synthesizes non-CompilerGenerated dummy fields on structs) and runs MessagePackGenerator on the defining project; CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync does neither.

`GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` still indexes `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` and casts to `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`. The doc comment claims it returns null for metadata, but for a metadata property it throws IndexOutOfRangeException. The argument is evaluated before the new location filter runs, so the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path (line 985) still crashes for a referenced type whose key is null. A record positional property would also make the cast invalid. No test covers this path.

The issue lists three `[0]` sites (original lines 735, 1009, 1101). The diff touches only the latter two. The site near original line 735 is not shown as changed and may still crash on metadata symbols in other shapes.

The filter drops every diagnostic whose location is not in source, including diagnostics about types in the current compilation that were created with a null or Location.None location (for example, when a GetIdentifierLocation-style helper returns null). This could silently hide existing user-visible diagnostics well beyond the metadata case.

The docs claim problems are reported by the defining assembly. That holds only if the defining assembly was itself built with the MessagePack analyzer, which a third-party NuGet package may not have been. In that case the problem is now silently ignored rather than reported anywhere.

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose location is not in the current compilation's syntax trees, which suppresses legitimate consumer-project errors when a valid generic [MessagePackObject] from a referenced assembly (e.g., Item<T> with [Key(0)] public T Value) is closed in the consumer with an unformattable metadata type (e.g., Item<System.IO.Stream>). Because both the member symbol (Item<Stream>.Value) and the field/property type (Stream) are metadata symbols with no syntax in the current compilation, the unformattable-type diagnostic gets Location.None and is silently dropped by the consumer while the defining assembly could never report it on open T. The same check also silently drops any current-compilation diagnostic whose nullable location helper (such as GetParameterListLocation at line 1454 on a null or implicitly declared constructor) returns null.

Both README.md line 1642 and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md line 52 assert that member diagnostics on referenced-assembly generic types are reported by the defining assembly, and TypeCollector.cs line 1446 drops them in the consumer on that assumption. However, libraries that only reference MessagePack.Annotations (without MessagePack / MessagePack.SourceGenerator) never run MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer when built, so unkeyed public members on generic types from MessagePack.Annotations-only assemblies are now reported by neither project while the consumer generates a formatter that silently omits those members.

out_of_scope.description: Global `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` filter wrapping all analyzer diagnostics. This is a broader policy change than replacing `[0]` indexing.
New documentation section on generic types from referenced assemblies.
New section describing a suppression policy for referenced types.
